the Red Sea noun

also Red Sea

classical

Plin. 2.168 (Lewis & Short s.v. Arabia)
Mel. 3.8.1 (Lewis & Short)
M-O s.v. seas: Red Sea (Mercator, 1595)

sinus Arabicus

The Arabian Gulf, the Romans’ name for what we call the Red Sea; their mare Rubrum was a wider sea, taking in the Persian Gulf and the Indian Ocean (M-O).

Other words

  • mare Rubrum

    also used · late Latin · Vulg. Exod. 13.18: per viam dēsertī quae est juxtā mare Rubrum; Tac. A. 14.25: ad lītora maris Rubrī; M-O s.v. seas: Red Sea (Trappen, 1843; Egger)

    The usual name today. Classically mare Rubrum was the wider sea east of Arabia (M-O), as in Nepos’ usque ā rubrō marī (Hann. 2.1, Lewis & Short s.v. usque) and in Tacitus; the Vulgate gives it to the sea of the Exodus, the Red Sea proper, and so it is labelled late in this sense.

See also Arabia, Egypt, Sinai, Indian Ocean, the Persian Gulf.
